title: Duke Falls Out of Top 25 After Humiliating Home Defeat to Illinois – CBS Sports Rankings Shock
body:
The Illinois Fighting Illini stunned the college basketball world on Tuesday night, routing the No. 1‑ranked Duke Blue Devils 99‑78 at Cameron Indoor Stadium. The 21‑point defeat not only handed the Blue Devils their second loss of the season but also sent them tumbling down the national rankings, while the Illini vaulted into the Top 25 with a statement win that could reshape the early‑season landscape.

Illinois entered the game riding a perfect 5‑0 record and a reputation for high‑tempo offense, but few expected the team to dominate a program that has long been synonymous with championship pedigree. From the opening tip, the Illini pressed aggressively, forcing turnovers and converting them into fast‑break points. Freshman guard Jaden Miller sparked the offense with a barrage of three‑pointers, finishing with 28 points on 11‑of‑18 shooting. Senior forward Marcus Hawthorne added a double‑double, contributing 16 points and 12 rebounds while anchoring the defensive effort that limited Duke’s star forward to just nine points.

Duke, ranked No. 1 in the AP and Coaches polls, looked out of sync from the outset. The Blue Devils struggled to find rhythm against Illinois’ relentless pressure, missing 15 of 32 attempts from beyond the arc and committing eight turnovers in the first half alone. Coach Mike Krzyzewski, who has guided Duke to five national titles, was forced to make multiple adjustments, but the Illini’s depth and athleticism proved too much. Senior guard Aidan Cole, who led the Blue Devils with 22 points, was kept off the floor for much of the second half after a hard foul on Miller resulted in a brief ejection, further hampering Duke’s offensive flow.

The loss marks a dramatic shift for both programs. Duke’s early‑season ranking had them perched atop the national polls, but the 99‑78 defeat dropped them out of the Top 5 in the latest Coaches poll and out of the Top 10 in the AP poll—a rare tumble for a team that has consistently been a fixture in the upper echelons of college basketball. The defeat also raises questions about Duke’s defensive schemes and its ability to adapt to high‑pressing opponents, a concern that will likely dominate preseason discussions and recruiting narratives.

For Illinois, the victory is a springboard that could catapult the Fighting Illini into serious national contention. Their 99 points represent the highest output of any team this season, and the win against a top‑ranked opponent validates the program’s recent recruiting successes, including a highly touted recruiting class that featured multiple five‑star prospects. Head coach Brad Underwood praised his squad’s execution, noting that “the guys stuck to the game plan, played with confidence, and never gave Duke a chance to get comfortable.” The Illini now sit at 6‑0 and are poised to climb even higher in the polls, potentially breaking into the Top 15 for the first time since the 2014‑15 season.

Looking ahead, both teams face pivotal matchups that could define their trajectories. Duke will travel to face the 15‑ranked Tennessee Volunteers next week, a contest that will test whether the Blue Devils can rebound from a humiliating loss and reassert their dominance. Illinois, meanwhile, returns home to host the 12‑ranked Purdue Boilermakers, a rivalry game that will further test the Illini’s consistency against elite competition. If Illinois can sustain the intensity displayed against Duke, they may emerge as a genuine contender for the Big Ten title and a deep run in the NCAA tournament. For Duke, the challenge will be to regroup, tighten their defense, and demonstrate that the early stumble is merely a blip on an otherwise storied season.
